name: half-log-two-log-and-exp-at-twelve-points
rationale: An owned fixture calling log2, log and exp on half4 once each, twelve points in all. These three families are 120 corpus sources apiece -- 360 together, the largest uncovered block after reverse_bits -- and no corpus host reaches them: in every one the call sits in a function-constant-gated region that folds away, so a CLI sweep sees them as never lowered. The log2 points are all powers of two, so 2, -2, 0 and 8 are exact and independent of any rounding the implementation chooses; the log and exp points are the correctly rounded half of the true value, which is what both back ends produce. Using the default rather than a precise:: spelling is deliberate: log, log2 and exp are the three half transcendentals measured byte-identical between the fast and precise variants over all 65536 halves, so the variant split that blocks tan, atan and asin does not apply here.

name: linked-single-invocation-zero-bin
rationale: One invocation is bounded by source_size 1x1. Linking is enabled with one authored texture and one address-table element; the exact callback is loop-free and returns float4 zero without dereferencing either resource. The one-bin histogram parameters force every active scalar lane to bin zero, and the poisoned counter makes the bounded global-atomic write observable byte-exactly.

name: linked-single-unpadded-write
rationale: One invocation is admitted by a 1x1 grid. The pad parameters' divisor words are 0x00010001, and padArrayData divides by their low halves (it reads no high half), so both divisors are one. Unit divisors and widths with zero left and right padding select source coordinate zero, the reference-size constant exposes one device-buffer slot, the linked prefix returns exact one, and the linked postfix writes that value to element zero.

name: sixteen-overlapping-triangles-update-a-raster-ordered-argument-buffer-member
rationale: Ordering evidence for a raster order group declared on an argument-buffer member (no fixture carried one). Buffer 0 is the 8-byte argument buffer Targets whose only member, acc (id 0, field offset 0), is a device uint pointer carrying raster_order_group(0) in its air.indirect_argument metadata; the executors encode the authored buffer's address there. The draw is 16 instances of the executors' fullscreen triangle on an 8x8 rgba8_unorm target, so sixteen fragments cover every pixel. Each fragment reads the uint word of its pixel (index 8 * uint(position.y) + uint(position.x)) and writes 3v + 1 back with a plain load and store; the word is in raster order group 0, which orders overlapping fragments' accesses, so each pixel's sixteen read-modify-writes run one after another. Word i starts at i, so it ends at 3^16 i + (3^16 - 1) / 2 (mod 2^32; 21523360 for pixel 0, 2733466783 for pixel 63), whatever order the identical fragments take: a lost update (two fragments reading the same value) leaves 3^15 i + (3^15 - 1) / 2 or less, and a pixel-index mix-up shows as the start value of another word. Instances cannot be told apart by the fragment, so this settles the ordering guarantee as mutual exclusion of the read-modify-write, not submission order. The color output is not observed. The AIR has no loop.

name: manual-half4-fetch-at-an-offset-transformed-onto-three-of-four-pixels
rationale: Reaching variant of this entry's manual-vertex-fetch case, whose zero constants gave a degenerate position. Constant 132 enables manual fetch; table slot 0 holds the same-library callback re::vertexfetch::fetchFromHalf4, and record 0 of the vertex-argument buffer (15 records of 24 bytes, the rest null) points at half4 positions with stride 8 and offset 8, which skips a leading decoy vertex (40, 40, 40). The three positions are (-1, -1), (3, -1), (-1, 3) with z = 1/4 with the matrix z scale 2, so world z = 5/8. The instance matrix (objectToCrWorld, column-major) scales x and y by 1/2, scales z and translates by (-1/4, -1/4, 1/8); crWorldToProjArray[0] keeps x, y and w and maps z to z/2 + 1/16, so the clip triangle is (-3/4, -3/4), (5/4, -3/4), (-3/4, 5/4) at w = 1. It covers the pixel centres (-1/2, 1/2), (-1/2, -1/2) and (1/2, -1/2) of the 2x2 target with a margin of at least 1/4 from every edge and misses (1/2, 1/2): pixel (1, 0) keeps its fill. The depth is the same at all three vertices, so its interpolation is exact; every product and sum is a small dyadic value, exact in float with or without contraction, and the observer writes (x + 1/2, y + 1/2, z, 1) for each covered pixel. screenSpaceDepthBias = 1/4 adds 1/4 * w to clip z: depth 0.625.

name: manual-vertex-fetch-null-buffer-defaults
no_effect: Zero instance and view constants give a degenerate position: the primitive covers no fragment, so the render target keeps its authored bytes.
rationale: Function constant 132 enables manual vertex fetch. Every zero-initialized embedded vertex-buffer pointer is null, so each AIR guard bypasses its table lookup and supplies the defined default attribute. Slot zero is the exact same-library invalid-format callback that supplies the table's required type but is unreachable. Clipping is disabled by function constant 35; its only structural backedge is capped by an unsigned 16-bit counter reaching 32. Zero transform constants produce a deterministic degenerate position. Buffer 30 and its reflected offset-zero device buffer are now authored explicitly; the invalid-format callback deterministically supplies the same default attribute when that first record is reached.

name: linked-single-threadgroup-zero-bin
rationale: One 1x1 threadgroup dispatches one invocation. kLogBinEntries=0 makes both initialization and flush loops contain exactly one bin, kTGSizeIs256=false uses the literal one-thread group size as their stride, and source_size=1x1 bounds the image path. The exact linked callback returns float4 zero without dereferencing resources; the poisoned global bin makes the local-atomic aggregation observable byte-exactly.

name: imageblock-three-widths-load
rationale: air.load.implicit_imageblock.f32, air.load.implicit_imageblock.f16, air.load.implicit_imageblock.i32 and air.store.implicit_imageblock.f32 had no authored case. One implicit imageblock with a float, a half and a uint member reaches every width of both families at once, because an implicit-layout imageblock member is its colour attachment and the three attachments can carry three different formats. The integer member is uint rather than int on purpose: AIR mangles both as i32, the attachment format is read off that suffix so reflection declares R32Uint for either, and the only corpus source that reaches this family declares a uint member too. The existing kernel_implicit_imageblock_half2 fixture copies the block to itself and observes a single 1x1 region, so it says nothing about the imageblock coordinate; here every thread writes its own row of the output buffer keyed by thread_position_in_threadgroup and every cell of the three attachments carries its own linear index, so a swapped or dropped coordinate is visible in all 256 cells of all three planes. The three write-backs use deliberately different arithmetic per width (+1.0f, *2.0h, +100) so a store that landed in the wrong plane could not be mistaken for a correct one. Every value is an exact integer or quarter, so no row depends on a rounding mode. This case observes the load side: all 256 cells of all three members, read through the imageblock and bit-cast into one uint buffer.

name: four-corner-block-span-past-tolerance-lowers-the-atomic-minimum
rationale: One thread at grid position (0, 0) reads four blocks and folds them into one atomic minimum. blockSize is 8 and BlockGrid::minBlockSize is 4, so the stride the kernel scales its thread position by is (8 >> 1) / 4 = 1, and with a 2x2 grid the four corner offsets (0,0), (1,0), (0,1) and (1,1) clamp to themselves and address blocks 0 through 3 -- every block the buffer holds, so the two clamps against w-1 and h-1 are exercised without any of them silently collapsing two corners onto one block. Their zMin values are 4, 8, 2, 16 and their zMax values 1, 32, 4, 8, so the reduction that starts at FLT_MAX and zero lands on 2 and 32: every value is a power of two and air.fast_fmin/air.fast_fmax are associative and commutative over them, so the loop's order is not part of the answer. Neither sentinel survives, which is what the two guards check, and the span of 30 clears a tolerance of 16, so air.atomic.global.min.u.i32 runs against a buffer holding 100 and leaves 8 -- a value that is the blockSize, is not the initial contents, and is not what an atomic max or an unconditional store would have written.

name: dsm2-zero-sign-lanes-zero-to-fifteen-live
rationale: Lanes 0-15 of one simdgroup of 32 run the multiply-add (live mask 0x0000ffff), on fragments every lane loaded before the branch; lanes 16-31 do not take part, and a probe measured their cells read as zero. Rows 0-3 (lanes 0-15) show that zero's sign z: rows 0-1 read z, rows 2-3 read -z. Inputs (S-): a is +1 everywhere except a[r][k] = -1 for rows 2-3, columns 4-7; b rows 0-3 are -0 and b rows 4-7 (the cells lanes 16-31 hold) are -0; c is -0. A whole simdgroup's result is -0 in rows 0, 1, 4-7 (every term -0) and +0 in rows 2-3 (-1 * -0 = +0). Rows 0-3 are held by lanes 0-15, and their terms in k = 4-7 multiply an a cell of lanes 0-15 by a b cell of lanes 16-31: if those b cells are a zero z, rows 0-1 read z * 1 = z and rows 2-3 read z * -1 = -z, every other term -0, so rows 0-1 are -0 and rows 2-3 +0 when z is -0, and the reverse when z is +0. Every value is +1, -1, +4, -4, or a signed zero, exact in float and half whatever the accumulation order, and a sum of signed zeros is -0 exactly when every term is. out[2g + j] is lane g's float cell j, out[2n + 2g + j] its half cell widened (n the grid's threads); a lane that does not run the multiply-add leaves its words at the 0xAB poison. Compiled without fast math. The AIR has no loop.

name: dsm2-zero-sign-lanes-zero-to-fifteen-live-plus-zero-rows
rationale: dsm2-zero-sign-lanes-zero-to-fifteen-live with input S+, whose b rows 4-7 (the cells lanes 16-31 loaded) are +0: the same bytes show the zero cell does not follow the loaded signed zeros. Inputs (S+): input S- with b rows 4-7 (the cells lanes 16-31 hold) +0 in place of -0: a whole simdgroup's rows 0-1 and 4-7 are +0 and rows 2-3 -0. Where lanes 16-31 do not take part, rows 0-1 read z and rows 2-3 read -z for their zero cell z, the same bytes as under S- unless the multiply-add reads those lanes' loaded registers. name: dsm2-zero-sign-odd-lanes-live
rationale: The odd lanes of one simdgroup of 32 run the multiply-add (live mask 0xaaaaaaaa); the even lanes, whose a cells the odd lanes' terms in k = 0, 1, 4, 5 read, do not take part. The zero's sign on the a side: columns 2-3 read z, columns 6-7 read -z. Inputs (O): a[r][k] is +1 in columns 0, 1, 4, 5 (the even lanes' a cells) and -0 in columns 2, 3, 6, 7; b[k][j] is -1 for k in {0, 1, 4, 5} and j in {6, 7}, else +1; c is -0. A whole simdgroup's result is -4 in columns 6-7 and +4 elsewhere. The odd lanes hold columns 2, 3, 6, 7, and their terms in k = 0, 1, 4, 5 multiply an even lane's a cell by an odd lane's b cell, the others are -0: if the even lanes' cells are a zero z, columns 2-3 read z and columns 6-7 read -z. name: visible-table-clear-slots-two-through-eight-simd-primary
rationale: One invocation calls visible-function-table slots 2 through 8 and receives exact float4 zero from all seven linked _uber_clear bodies. A ten-word size table and eight explicit argument-info records keep every selector and offset in bounds; register 2 is selected. The entry writes that result to the poisoned primary texel before subgroup aggregation, and binding zero is captured byte-exactly.

name: nchw-signed-int8-weights-six-columns-dilated-taps-and-channel-remainder
rationale: Reaching variant of this entry's zero-extent case. Constant 115 = 0x20000140300 selects float data with signed 8-bit weights (weights code 1, bits 10 and 11 clear) and float weight scales read from table entry 2, NCHW source and destination, data tile 4, weights tile 4 and channel tile 4; constant 122 = 0x10101 gives the table three arrays (0 data, 1 destination, 2 scales). The parameters (binding 29): 5 input channels and one output channel in one group, a 3 x 2 kernel, batch 1, an 8 x 1 source and a 6 x 1 destination, offsets (-1, -1), strides (1, 1), dilations (2, 1), source element strides (1, 8, 8, 40) and weight strides (30, 6, 1, 3) (output channel, input channel, kx, ky). The kernel parameters (binding 23) hold one 80-byte entry per table array, so they are 240 bytes; entry 2 gives the scale stride 1. Two threads (one threadgroup) each own four destination columns: thread 0 columns 0 to 3, thread 1 columns 4 and 5, its columns 6 and 7 failing the destination bound. The kernel row ky = 0 reads source row -1 and is skipped; taps left of 0 or past column 7 are skipped; the five channels take a full channel tile and a one-channel remainder whose other lanes load zero; the weights tile's channels 1 to 3 fail the output-channel bound and load zero. The linked writer (postfixPrimary_f, module aad641ec) stores coordinate (x, 0, 0, 0) at word x of array 1, so each column lands on its own word. Data ((3i + 1) mod 7) - 3, or 4 where that is zero; weights ((5i + 2) mod 15) - 7, or 8 where that is zero (two's complement bytes); scale 0.25. Expected array 1: [15.5, 10.0, 3.25, 2.25, -9.75, 0.25] and two words keeping 0xab. Every product is an integer of magnitude at most 32 and every sum is below 2^9 before the exact scaling by 0.25, so every word is exact in any summation order; no output is zero. Every loop is bounded by these parameters (two kernel rows, three taps, two channel tiles, four columns, four output channels).

name: ndarray-quantized-conv-zero-output-channels
no_effect: The authored parameters give the work an empty extent, so the entry returns before any write reaches the selected output.
rationale: One invocation selects the float quantized-convolution specialization with unit geometry and a zero output-channel count. The pre-write channel guard exits before MPS NDArray construction or data dereference; all declared resources nevertheless satisfy the entry ABI, while the four poisoned observed bytes remain unchanged. Replaced: the linked destination callback writes table entry 1, so the case binds a two-entry table (MPSNDArrayRefSize 1 source, 1 destination) whose destination element carries the source element's fill.

name: nhwc-unsigned-8-bit-weights-half-scales-seven-output-channels
rationale: Reaching variant of this entry's zero-extent case, the NHWC counterpart of the NCHW variant. Constant 115 = 0x20001120f05 selects an NHWC source (bits 0-1 = 1) and destination (bits 2-3 = 1), float data, weights code 7 (8-bit, bits 10 and 11 set: unsigned), half weight scales read from table entry 2, data tile 4, weights tile 4 and channel tile 8; constant 122 = 0x10101 gives the table three arrays. The parameters (binding 29): 3 input and 7 output channels in one group, a 2 x 2 kernel, batch 1, a 2 x 1 source and a 1 x 1 destination, offsets (0, -1), unit strides and dilations, source strides (1, 3, 6, 6) (channel, x, row, batch, as the NHWC path permutes them) and weight strides (1, 7, 21, 42) (output channel, input channel, kx, ky). The 240-byte kernel parameters (binding 23) give entry 2 the scale stride 1, so output channel k takes scale k. With an NHWC source the thread's x index selects the output channels: thread 0 owns channels 0 to 3 (one four-wide weight load per input channel, since channel 3 < 7) and thread 1 channels 4 to 7 (scalar loads; channel 7 fails the bound and loads zero). The kernel row ky = 0 reads source row -1 and is skipped; the three channels fill part of the 8-channel tile and the rest load zero; data-tile columns 1 to 3 fail the destination bound. The linked writer (postfixPrimary_f, module aad641ec) stores coordinate (k, 0, 0, 0) at word k of array 1, one word per output channel. Data ((3i + 2) mod 9) - 4, or 5 where that is zero; weight bytes (37i + 11) mod 256, or 1 where that is zero; scales [0.5, 0.25, 2.0, 1.0, 0.125, 4.0, 0.75] (half). Expected array 1: [127.5, 119.25, 1398.0, 921.0, 142.875, 5460.0, -153.75] and word 7 keeping 0xab. Every product is an integer of magnitude at most 1275, every sum is below 2^13, and every scale is a multiple of 1/8, so every word is exact in any summation order; no output is zero. Every loop is bounded by these parameters.

name: bounded-dynamic-visible-table-clear-slot-two-dual-output
rationale: The literal four-word size table [4, 0, 0, 0] bounds the only reachable loop: its induction starts at visible-table slot 2, increments once to 3, and exits because the masked first word minus one is exactly 3. One invocation takes the non-empty path because the authored bounds are float2(1), calls visible-function-table slot 2, and receives exact float4 zero from the linked _uber_clear body. Eight explicit argument-info records keep every selector and offset in bounds, with register 2 selected as the result. This entry swizzles that result to float4(0,0,0,1), writes both required poisoned output textures, and selects binding zero for byte-exact comparison.

name: visible-table-clear-slots-two-through-fourteen-simd-primary
rationale: One invocation calls visible-function-table slots 2 through 14 and receives exact float4 zero from all thirteen linked _uber_clear bodies. name: visible-table-clear-slots-two-through-twenty-threadgroup-primary

name: linked-zero-work-wavematch-multiple-threadgroup-histogram
no_effect: The zeroed wave-match parameters select no histogram work, so the destination keeps its authored bytes.
rationale: The zeroed wave-match parameter record yields no histogram work for the one-thread dispatch; the retained destination stays byte-exact. All five direct visible references use established modules with their matching scalar ABI signatures.

name: wavematch-histogram-float-keys-intermediate-source-stride-two
rationale: Reaching variant of the zero-work case of this entry, whose zero sort extent leaves the histogram unwritten. Constant 124 = 0x80 selects float keys, ascending, no argsort, and the intermediate source: keys are read from tempBuffer1 (binding 28) through the parameter record's second stride set (stride 2, so the interleaved values 3, 4, ... at odd slots must be skipped), not through the constant linked source. One threadgroup of 32 lanes (one simdgroup, 16 elements a lane) ranks 40 keys, +-2^e for e in -4..4: each key's bits are flipped to radix order (sign set for positives, all bits inverted for negatives) and digit (flipped >> 23) & 255, the biased exponent for a positive key and 255 minus it for a negative one, counts into the 256-bin threadgroup histogram through threadgroup atomic adds, which the threadgroup then writes to tempBuffer5 (binding 24) with bin stride 1: all 256 words are written, nonzero bins {123: 4, 124: 4, 125: 4, 126: 5, 127: 5, 128: 4, 129: 4, 130: 5, 131: 4, 132: 1}. Integer counts are exact in any atomic order. Every loop is finite: the zeroing and write loops run 256 / 32 steps, the element loops 16.

name: a-thread-reads-its-own-write-after-a-texture-barrier-without-sparseness
rationale: The control of the barrier write case (a-write-to-an-unmapped-texel-read-back-after-a-texture-barrier): the same AIR and probes on a texture that is not sparse. Texture 0 is 256x128 r32_float with texel (x, y) = 1000y + x + 1 (exact), not sparse. Thread i runs probe i of buffer 0 (32 bytes: kind, x, y, 0, then a float4 value) and writes out[2i] = the raw bits of the float4 sparse_read of texel (x, y) and out[2i+1] = (resident() ? 1 : 0, kind, i, 0x5A5); kind 0 first writes the value at (x, y) and fences the texture, kind 1 does not; every thread (one threadgroup) then reaches threadgroup_barrier(mem_flags::mem_texture) before its read. Each probe addresses its own texel. Probes: 0 read (5, 7); 1 write 42.5 at (6, 7) and read it; 2 write 43.5 at (200, 7) and read it; 3 read (201, 7), never written; 4 write 44.5 at (256, 7), past the width, and read it; 5 write 45.5 at (127, 127); 6 write 46.5 at (128, 127); 7 write 47.5 at (5, 128), past the height; 8 read (129, 127), beside probe 6's write. The value written is (v, 1, 2, 3) and r32_float keeps v. Texture 0 is an out-of-bounds target of the texture form. The output is pre-filled with 0xAB; the AIR has no loop.

name: a-write-to-an-unmapped-texel-read-back-after-a-texture-barrier
rationale: What a write to an unmapped texel of a sparse texture does on Metal, observed by the writing thread after a texture fence and a threadgroup barrier on texture memory, since a fence alone did not show the thread its own write of a mapped texel. The texture is an input declared read_write by the function, so the oracle makes it with shader read and write usage, and the Vulkan candidate a storage image. A sparse texture is made on Metal from a sparse heap of 16 KiB pages and mapped with MTLResourceStateCommandEncoder before the work, and on Vulkan as a sparse resident image bound with vkQueueBindSparse; Only the mapped texels' authored bytes are uploaded. Each region is a whole number of tiles on every device that runs the case (an executor refuses a region that is not whole tiles of its device), so the mapped texels are the same wherever the case runs; each run prints its tiling. Texture 0 is 256x128 r32_float with texel (x, y) = 1000y + x + 1 (exact) and its left 128x128 mapped (x 128..255 unmapped). Thread i runs probe i of buffer 0 (32 bytes: kind, x, y, 0, then a float4 value) and writes out[2i] = the raw bits of the float4 sparse_read of texel (x, y) and out[2i+1] = (resident() ? 1 : 0, kind, i, 0x5A5); kind 0 first writes the value at (x, y) and fences the texture, kind 1 does not; every thread (one threadgroup) then reaches threadgroup_barrier(mem_flags::mem_texture) before its read. Each probe addresses its own texel. Probes: 0 read (5, 7); 1 write 42.5 at (6, 7) and read it; 2 write 43.5 at (200, 7) and read it; 3 read (201, 7), never written; 4 write 44.5 at (256, 7), past the width, and read it; 5 write 45.5 at (127, 127); 6 write 46.5 at (128, 127); 7 write 47.5 at (5, 128), past the height; 8 read (129, 127), beside probe 6's write. The value written is (v, 1, 2, 3) and r32_float keeps v. Texture 0 is an out-of-bounds target of the texture form. The output is pre-filled with 0xAB; the AIR has no loop.

name: volatile-load-of-a-program-scope-constant-array-element
rationale: Four threads each add their index to a volatile load of table[1] = (5, 6, 7, 8), element 1 of a program-scope constant uint4 array, at a constant index. The compiler folds an ordinary load of a constant initializer, so only the volatile load keeps a load of the closed constant object in the AIR, which the engine lowers as access.constant.load (a read-only typed constant object carries no Volatile). out[t] = (5 + t, 6 + t, 7 + t, 8 + t); every selected byte differs from the 0xab fill. The AIR has no loop.

name: block-read-array-1x2

Each of the 84 threads reads the block at a point and level of its row and stores one of its two texels: points inside, at and past each edge, negative, and INT_MIN; levels 0 and 1, past the last (2 and 5) and -1.

name: sign-of-zero-and-division-range-under-fast-math
rationale: The residue left to the comparison classes: the zero's sign from sign under nsz, and the range of Metal's division. Sign: the product lowers sign under nsz as FSign, because Metal wrote +0 for w - lr * (sign(w) * s + g) at w = -0 in the private d72f0f18, where the exact sequence gives -0. The mechanism was not isolated. Here sign(w) and that step are read at signed zeros, denormals, +-1, +-0.5, infinities, NaNs, the largest finite, and the smallest normals (lr = 0.5, s = 1, g = +0), plus eight lanes with other lr, s, and g (a negative-zero g, a negative lr, s = 2 or -1, g = 0.5 or 1). The half sign gets the analogous values. Division: fdiv of dividends whose exact quotient is a normal (or a special) by the divisors 2^126, 1.5 * 2^126, 2^127, 1.5 * 2^127, the largest finite, -2^127, 2^-126, 2^-127, and 2^-149, plus 3, 1, +-0, and inf. The half division uses 2^14, 2^15, 65504, 2^-14, 2^-15, and 2^-24. Metal's fast division bounds its error only for divisors in [2^-126, 2^126]; its reciprocal flushed past them is why fast_tanh answers 0 near x = 44. A correctly rounded OpFDiv gives the exact quotient. Thread i writes the word group 4i..4i+3: sign(w), the step, n / d, and the half sign(x) | (n / d) << 16. There are 24 sign lanes, 36 float and 26 half division lanes, and 48 threads; the padding is w = 2 and n / d = 2 / 1. Compiled with the default fast math, as the corpus is: sign, the step's arithmetic, and both divisions carry fast. sign-of-zero-and-division-range-without-fast-math is the same program compiled -fno-fast-math.
